newsitem.title: European Union: 171254 OEC - BC-TEXT-RAPID-SAFRICA EU, S. Africa progress in bilateral agreement negotiations.
newsitem.headline: 171254 OEC - BC-TEXT-RAPID-SAFRICA EU, S. Africa progress in bilateral agreement negotiations.

text.p: EUROPEAN COMMISSION PRESS RELEASE: IP/97/226 DOCUMENT DATE: MARCH 17, 1997 * EU and South Africa make progress in the negotiations for a bilateral agreement * On 13 and 14 March 1997, representatives of the Republic of South Africa and the European Commission met again in Brussels for ongoing technical discussions on the proposed long term framework for cooperation between South Africa and the European Union. Having finalized at the previous session the technical work on the Lome Protocol, which will give South Africa qualified membership of the ACP-EU Convention, technical discussions took place this time on the proposed EU/South Africa bilateral agreement. Two groups of issues were discussed: overall objectives and general provisions and trade-related aspects of the future bilateral agreement. In both areas, in-depth exchanges took place, which resulted in the identification of substantial common ground, as well as areas on which further research and discussion will be required. Both sides noted that development of South and Southern Africa should feature high amongst the overall objectives of the agreement. They stressed the importance of considering respect for human rights and democratic principles, as well as the principles of good governance and the rule of law as essential elements of the agreement.The discussion also focused on matters relating to structured political dialogue. A number of trade-related issues were discussed, ranging from safeguard, anti-dumping and countervailing action, intellectual property to competition policy, public procurement and the free movement of capital. Broad agreement was noted on the need to address such issues in the context of the future agreement and on the principles that should guide negotiations on each of them. Further in-depth discussions will need to take place on these issues. At the same time, the right of each party to the development of its own legislation was recognized. The need for consistency between future bilateral undertakings on such matters and the commitments already entered into under GATT/WTO and other multilateral arrangements was also underlined. The next round of technical discussions will be held in early May, and will concentrate on development co-operation issues. END OF DOCUMENT.
